body:
Maya (Sales): ACME POC: customer keeps getting 413 when they POST the full session transcript. They claim ~12.5MB JSON. Client prints HTTP/1.1 413. Can we make a quick playbook for them?
Carlos (SE): 413 indicates our ingress/gateway rejected the body. Ask for raw response + a sanitized sample request body. Also ask which region/endpoint they're hitting.
Maya (Sales): Theyre on hosted us-east-1. Pasted their console log:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  --data-binary @transcript.json

> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> Content-Length: 13107200

< HTTP/1.1 413 Request Entity Too Large
< server: envoy
< content-type: application/json

{"error":"request too large","code":"PayloadTooLarge"}
```
Jamal (Support): That's consistent with our public gateway limit (~10MB). We count raw request bytes before any model-side token checks. Which means we have to solve the transport first.
Anya (SalesOps): Customer asked if we can just bump the limit for a few days for the POC. Whats the ops path?
Priya (Eng Oncall): For hosted public API we don't do per-customer prod gateway config changes. Options:
- Short term: use a pointer/upload flow (recommended) or chunking/summarization (no infra change).
- Medium term: provision a Dedicated POC environment with higher ingress (requires billing + ~2-4 business days).
- Investigate temporary internal bypass routing but that'll need infra & security approvals (multi-day). I'll open a ticket to check feasibility.
Liu (Platform Eng): Confirming gateway enforces 10,485,760 byte limit in us-east cluster. We have an upload endpoint (/v1/upload) that accepts larger objects and stores them to internal S3; customers can then pass a signed reference to /v1/generate. That avoids changing global gateway limits.
Maya (Sales): Can you paste an example of the upload + pointer pattern to share with ACME? They want a code snippet.
Carlos (SE): Example flow (sanitized):
```bash
# 1) Upload transcript (POST to our upload endpoint)
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/upload" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -F "file=@transcript.json"
# response: {"upload_id":"abc123", "signed_url":"https://s3-presigned-url"}

# 2) Call generate with pointer to uploaded transcript
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"transcript_ref":"upload:abc123","last_n":10}'
```
Carlos (SE): If theyre running a client that can't do multipart/form-data, presigned S3 upload also works: we return a presigned PUT URL from /v1/upload and they PUT directly to S3, then call /v1/generate with the object reference.
Nikhil (Security): Presigned uploads are allowed but we need to confirm retention and encryption requirements for the customer. If they require customer-managed KMS or specific residency, that's additional SOW.
Jamal (Support): Other on-the-wire tricks: clients can gzip the payload (Content-Encoding: gzip) - but only supported on /v1/upload, not on /v1/generate in prod gateway. Also Transfer-Encoding: chunked does not bypass the size limit.
Maya (Sales): ACME says they want end-to-end fidelity during the POC (can't summarize). If we propose Dedicated, what's the rough POC pricing and lead time?
Anya (SalesOps): For a short Dedicated POC with increased ingress we normally quote a daily infra add-on + reserved slot. Quick internal ballpark: ~$1,500/day plus standard reserved capacity billing. Exact number depends on GPU type/throughput; I'll put together a formal quote if they want to proceed.
Priya (Eng Oncall): I've opened INF-4387 to capture logs & approvals and to validate quick bypass options. Jamal/SE please attach the sanitized transcript + the client's IP and request_len from their logs.
Jamal (Support): Attached to INF-4387. Gateway log excerpt:
```
[2026-11-05T09:03:12Z] cluster=us-east1 client=34.72.11.8 request_len=13107200 limit=10485760 result=413 route=/v1/generate
```
Carlos (SE): Also note: even if we get the raw bytes through, the model has a finite token window. If the transcript maps to more tokens than the chosen model supports, they still need a strategy: long-context model, rolling-window, or local summarization. Recommend we ask for (a) estimated token count and (b) which model variant they plan to use.
Maya (Sales): I'll ask ACME for token mapping and whether they can accept a pointer workflow for the POC while we spin up a Dedicated test if needed.
Nikhil (Security): If they accept the presigned upload approach, we should add a short security checklist: encryption at rest, narrow presigned TTL, audit logs enabled. I can run that checklist with the customer if they want.
Liu (Platform Eng): TL;DR options for customer: 1) Upload to /v1/upload / presigned S3 + pass reference (fastest, lowest ops), 2) Chunk/stitch locally (engineering work on client side), 3) Dedicated POC with higher ingress (sales + ops, ~2-4d), 4) Temporary bypass (investigate; slower and needs approvals).
Maya (Sales): Great. I'll present those 4 options, include INF-4387, and ask for token estimate. Thanks everyone.
deploy-bot: Ticket INF-4387 created by Priya (Eng Oncall)
